name: Hu Wei Cheng Qi Tang
summary: A gentle purgative formula from the Warm Disease school that clears residual Heat from the Stomach and Intestines while nourishing Yin to protect the Stomach. It is used for constipation, dry mouth, and thirst that occur after a feverish illness, when Heat has damaged the body's fluids.
categories: ["Simultaneously attacking and tonifying formulas", "Purgative formulas", "Yin-enriching and Dryness-moistening formulas"]
tcm_actions: ["Purges Heat and unblocks bowels", "Nourishes Yin and moistens Dryness", "Protects Stomach Yin", "Descends Stomach Qi"]
pregnancy: Contraindicated during pregnancy. Contains Sheng Da Huang (生大黄, Rhubarb) which strongly purges and may stimulate uterine contractions, and Dan Pi (丹皮, Moutan) which moves Blood. Do not use during pregnancy.
breastfeeding: No specific data on safety during breastfeeding. Caution is advised as purgative herbs may affect the infant's digestion. Consult a healthcare provider before use.
children: Can be used in children at appropriately reduced doses. Reported in pediatric acute gastroenteritis and food accumulation constipation. Dosage must be adjusted by a qualified practitioner based on age and weight.
drug_interactions: No well-documented drug interactions. Caution is advised when combined with other purgatives or diuretics, as they may increase fluid loss and electrolyte imbalance. Consult a healthcare provider before concurrent use with prescription medications.
best_time_to_take: Take on an empty stomach in the morning for best purgative effect, or as directed by a practitioner.
typical_duration: Short-term use only; discontinue once bowel movement occurs. Usually taken for 1–3 days.
dietary_advice: Avoid cold, raw, and greasy foods while taking this formula. These foods can counteract the formula's action or further weaken the Spleen and Stomach. Light, warm, easily digestible foods are recommended.

ingredients.organ_affinity: Spleen, Stomach, Large Intestine, Liver, Pericardium
ingredients.role_description: Purges Heat and unblocks the bowels to eliminate accumulated Heat in the Stomach and Intestines.

ingredients.taste: Sweet (甘 gān), Bitter (苦 kǔ), Salty (咸 xián)
ingredients.role_description: Nourishes Yin and clears Heat, protecting Stomach Yin while supporting the purgative action.
Cools Blood and nourishes Yin, moistening dryness and protecting Stomach Yin.
Clears Heat and cools Blood, addressing residual Heat in the Blood level and preventing further Yin damage.
Clears Heat and nourishes Yin, moistens dryness and generates fluids to protect Stomach Yin.
Nourishes Yin and generates fluids, especially for Stomach Yin deficiency with dry mouth and throat.
